marks.gloss_en: כתיב הכא ונואלו וכתיב התם אשר נואלנו ואשר חטאנו -- as 'noalnu' there is joined to sin, so 'venoalu' here: those who study alone also sin
ואיבעית אימא מהכא: נואלו שרי צען... התעו את מצרים -- noalu joined to leading astray
and moreover they sin: 'venoalu' here, 'that we have been foolish (noalnu) and that we have sinned' there (Num 12:11)
והיינו דאמר רבי יוסי בר חנינא: חרב על... העוסקין בד בבד בתורה
R' Yosei bar Chanina: 'a sword upon the baddim, and they shall become fools' (Jer 50:36) -- a sword on the [enemies of the] scholars who study alone, and moreover they grow foolish
והיינו דאמר רבי חנינא: ... ומתלמידי יותר מכולן
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: why is Torah likened to wood (Prov 3:18)? as small wood kindles the large, small scholars sharpen the great
כדאמרה ליה ברתיה דקיסר לרבי יהושע בן חנניה -- the wine kept in gold and silver turned sour
the emperor's daughter to R' Yehoshua ben Chananya: alas, glorious wisdom in an ugly vessel
והא איכא שפירי דגמירי -- but there are handsome people who are learned
R' Yehoshua ben Chananya: does your father keep wine in clay vessels?... [the wine put in gold and silver turned sour] -- as she said to me, so I said to her
Rav Pappa: therefore let us say both: 'God of thanksgivings' and 'abundance of thanksgivings'
R' Abbahu: the day of rain is greater than the resurrection of the dead
Rav Yehuda: the day of rain is as great as the day the Torah was given -- 'my teaching (likchi) shall drop as the rain' (Deut 32:2), and lekach is Torah (Prov 4:2)
Rava set 'shall drop (yaarof) as the rain' against 'shall distil as the dew' (Deut 32:2): if he is a worthy scholar -- like dew; if not -- it breaks his neck like rain
R' Bena'a: whoever engages in Torah for its own sake, his Torah becomes an elixir of life for him (Prov 3:18; 3:8; 8:35)

R' Yochanan: 'for man is a tree of the field' (Deut 20:19) -- is man a tree? rather: 'you may eat of it and not cut it down' vs 'it you may destroy and cut down' (20:20): a worthy scholar -- eat of him and do not cut him down; if not -- destroy and cut down
R' Chama b. R' Chanina: 'iron sharpens iron' (Prov 27:17) -- as one iron sharpens another, two scholars sharpen each other in halakha
Rabba bar bar Chana: why is Torah likened to fire (Jer 23:29)? as fire does not burn alone, Torah is not retained by one alone
R' Chanina bar Pappa set Isa 21:14 against Isa 55:1: a worthy student -- bring the water to him; if not -- let the thirsty go to the water
R' Chanina bar Chama set Prov 5:16 against 5:17: a worthy student -- let your springs spread abroad; if not -- let them be yours alone
R' Chanina bar Idi: why is Torah likened to water (Isa 55:1)? as water leaves a high place for a low one, Torah is retained only by one whose mind is lowly
R' Oshaya: why is Torah likened to water, wine and milk (Isa 55:1)? as these keep only in the least of vessels, Torah is retained only by one whose mind is lowly
